cards.title: Doctor asks 'kya hua?' Then what?
cards.body: Most of us start with a long story from last Diwali. A clear 30 second version helps the doctor think faster and ask better follow-up questions.

cards.title: Start with the main problem
cards.body: One line. 'Dizziness when she stands up' beats 'she has been feeling off'. Say the thing that made you book the appointment.

cards.title: Then say when it started
cards.body: Since when, and is it getting better, worse or staying the same? 'Three days, worse in the mornings' tells the doctor a lot in a few words.

cards.title: How often, and how bad
cards.body: Once a day or all day? Mild, or stopping her from doing normal things? Simple words work fine. You don't need medical terms.

cards.title: What makes it better or worse
cards.body: After food, after walking, at night, after a new medicine? Patterns are clues. Mention anything you already tried, including home remedies.

cards.title: Mention new medicines and recent changes
cards.body: Any new tablet, a changed dose, a few missed days, a recent fever or fall. Things that seem unrelated sometimes are not.

cards.title: Practise it once in the auto
cards.body: Say it out loud on the way. Problem, since when, how often, what changes it, any medicine changes. Then let the doctor lead.

takeaway: Main problem, since when, how often, what changes it and any medicine changes: a clear symptom story in 30 seconds.
share: Explaining symptoms to a doctor? Problem, since when, how often, what changes it, new medicines.
